All of which is to say that, as familiar as I am with the tale and the songs, I really didn't know how it would play out on stage for Music Theatre Works. It turns out that MTW is presenting the latest version of the play, adapted just last year by David Lee.
The show, which has undergone some heavy cuts, sometimes feels rushed, but the players and production team know where to find Camelot’s real heart.
However, for this writer it felt like a spark was missing; something that drove the intensity of this love triangle home.

But for a beloved, well-known story that most audiences have come to equate with overblown romantic splendor and a huge, colorful cast in colorful Medieval costumes, this “Camelot” will probably disappoint.
Trying to invent a new, off-beat version is too difficult a task.
Christine Mayland Perkins as Queen Guinevere who leads with beautiful vocals. She shines every time she is on stage.

However, current audiences might look beyond scale and appreciated director Brianna Borger's focus on ideals clashing with desires. DETAILS: "Camelot" presented by Music Theater Works, runs now through Nov. 13, 2022 at the North Shore Center for the Performing Arts, 9501.

I am sorry to say that this is not up to the usual standards that Music Theater Works has set for itself, but it is a nice show with great music and will bring back some wonderful memories of the 1960's- The Kennedy Years!

cn.t: This pared-down Camelot receives mixed reviews, with critics praising Christine Mayland Perkins' vocals and the iconic Lerner and Loewe score, but questioning the spare production and unconventional directorial choices.
